slides.title: std::vector Overview
slides.prompt: std::vector is a sequence container representing a dynamic contiguous array. It manages memory automatically, expanding capacity when the array size exceeds current allocation.

slides.title: Adding Elements
slides.prompt: Fill in the function used to append an element to the end of a vector.

slides.title: Size vs Capacity
slides.prompt: What is the difference between vector size() and capacity()?
options: size() is the number of elements held; capacity() is the total memory allocated before requiring reallocation
capacity() is the number of elements held; size() is the maximum limit
There is no difference; both return the same value always
size() measures bytes; capacity() measures element count
slides.correctAnswer: size() is the number of elements held; capacity() is the total memory allocated before requiring reallocation

slides.title: Reserving Capacity
slides.prompt: Fill in the method used to pre-allocate memory for a vector to avoid frequent reallocations.
slides.codeSnippet:
std::vector<int> v;
v.___(1000); // Pre-allocate space for 1000 elements

slides.title: In-Place Construction
slides.prompt: Why is emplace_back() often preferred over push_back() for complex objects?
options: emplace_back constructs the object directly in vector memory, avoiding unnecessary copy/move operations
emplace_back guarantees O(1) performance while push_back is O(N)
emplace_back allows adding multiple elements at once
push_back works only for primitive data types
slides.correctAnswer: emplace_back constructs the object directly in vector memory, avoiding unnecessary copy/move operations

slides.title: Safe Element Access
slides.prompt: Fill in the method that performs bounds checking when accessing a vector element.
slides.codeSnippet: int val = vec.___(2); // Throws std::out_of_range if index is invalid

slides.title: Iterator Invalidation
slides.prompt: When are iterators to a vector invalidated during an insertion?
options: When size reaches capacity and reallocation to a new memory block occurs
On every call to push_back() regardless of capacity
Never; vector iterators remain valid indefinitely
Only when elements are erased from the vector
slides.correctAnswer: When size reaches capacity and reallocation to a new memory block occurs
